scope: Proposition 4.3 (Finite compatible jets) of the manuscript “A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf” (preprints/A-singular-normal-affine-surface-with-free-tangent-sheaf-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 048 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 48b1a74d3131e97b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the data of Propositions 2.3 and 3.3, there are finitely many holomorphic disk-to-outside transition germs, each a composition of flows (4.7) of orders 1, . . . , 7, together with holomorphic local rows Ak, Bk for 0 ≤ k ≤ 7, such that: the transitions fix C and preserve its conormal bundle L; the vector fields (4.3) match through row index seven; and A ∧ B = t2(1 + O(t)) on every chart. On any surface neighborhood Y realizing these transition germs, write I = OY (−C) and F = TY (− log C). The rows give two sections of F/I9F, lying in IF/I9F. Their determinant has leading term t4Et ∧ ∂z, equivalently t5∂t ∧ ∂z, with coefficient one.
